course.note: The offered skills equal the skills the documented rule selects (technical, quote found, one per skill key, priority order). A regression check on the rule, not a quality measure.
The skipped count equals the technical entries whose quote was not found.
Determinate labels: whether the skill was offered matches the authored eligible_expected.

e1.note: Share of authored JD skills found in the supplied extraction.

e1.unavailable_reason: the labels do not establish that the authored skill list is exhaustive, so false positives cannot be identified
the labels do not establish that the authored skill list is exhaustive, so false positives cannot be identified

e2.note: QUALIFIED agreement, determinate labels only. An ABSENT counts correct when it is a genuine absence OR its provenance is unknown (raw output not supplied/readable), so it can include absences that were really parser-dropped entries. Read it with status_agreement_strict. ABSENT caused by a rejected raw entry is not counted correct.

STRICT agreement: as status_agreement, but an ABSENT with unknown provenance is excluded from the denominator (reason absence_provenance_unknown) instead of being credited. Supply the raw string to make those cases scorable.
Labels authored missing or partial: share the model flagged at all (any status).

Labels authored demonstrated that the model flagged as a gap anyway (unsupported flags). A rejected raw no_gap is not a flag. It is 0 for an output that flags nothing, so read it with gap_detection_recall.
Missing versus partial, strict: the emitted status equals the authored truth. Lenient alternatives in acceptable_outcomes are NOT applied here; see status_agreement.
The emitted tier is the single authored tier.
The emitted tier is any member of an authored ambiguous set. Kept apart from the determinate metric.
Matched entries whose JD quote was found in the job description (the parser's own flag).
Matched entries whose JD quote contains (or is contained in) an authored JD anchor.
Matched entries that carry a resume quote and whether the parser found it in the resume text.

limitations: Scores describe only the supplied outputs. They are not a measurement of a live model unless the outputs were produced by one, and then only for these hand-authored scenarios.
Pooled rates sum numerators and denominators across 10 hand-authored scenarios. They are descriptive; per-scenario results are listed beside them and must be read with them.
Precision and F1 are unavailable for E1 because the labels do not establish an exhaustive skill list.
Only the eligibility rule is scored, on the supplied normalised output. Whether recommended courses are relevant or good is not measured and no recommender or YouTube call is made.
label_eligibility_agreement is downstream of E2: a gap the model did not flag shows up there as well.

metrics.note: The offered skills equal the skills the documented rule selects (technical, quote found, one per skill key, priority order). A regression check on the rule, not a quality measure.
The skipped count equals the technical entries whose quote was not found.
Determinate labels: whether the skill was offered matches the authored eligible_expected.
